name: Close-Grip Bench Press
why: Heavy press for your triceps.
setup: Lie flat, hands about shoulder-width.
Elbows close to your body.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety bars or use a spotter.
avoid: Hands so close your wrists bend.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

preferred.why: Heaviest loadable triceps lift; strength is specific to the lift trained.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press
why: Close press with the bent bar: easier on the wrists.
setup: Lie flat, hands on the inner grips.
Elbows close to your body.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
why: One dumbbell pressed with both hands: triceps press.
setup: Lie on a bench, one dumbbell held in both palms over your chest.
form: Lower the dumbbell to your chest, elbows close.
Press up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbell on your chest

name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
why: Close press on a fixed track: safe to push hard.
setup: Bench so the bar comes down on your lower chest.
Hands about shoulder-width, elbows close.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety stops just below your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press
why: Bench press with palms facing you.
setup: Lie flat, hands about shoulder-width, palms facing you.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Go lighter than your normal bench.
avoid: Going without a spotter or safeties.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Barbell Floor Press
why: Bench press lying on the floor: the top half, heavy.
setup: Lie on the floor in a rack, bar on the hooks over your chest.
Shoulder blades back, knees bent.
form: Lower until your upper arms touch the floor.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the rack safeties just above your chest.
avoid: Bouncing your elbows off the floor.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → upper arms on the floor

name: One-arm Barbell Floor Press
heavyWhy: one arm, balance limits the load
why: Floor press with one hand on the bar's middle.
setup: Lie on the floor, knees bent.
Have a partner hand you the bar, palm facing in.
form: Lower until your elbow touches the floor.
Press up until your arm is straight.
avoid: Letting the bar tip to one side.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight → elbow on the floor

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
why: Dumbbell press lying on the floor.
setup: Lie on the floor, knees bent, dumbbells over your chest.
form: Lower until your upper arms touch the floor.
Press up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Bouncing your elbows off the floor.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → upper arms on the floor

name: JM Press
why: Half close press, half skullcrusher.
setup: Lie flat, close grip, bar over your upper chest.
Elbows pointing toward your feet.
form: Bend the elbows and lower the bar toward your chin.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Dropping the bar onto your face.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar above your chin

name: Smith Machine JM Press
heavyWhy: mostly triceps, not a big-muscle lift
why: JM press on a fixed track: easy to focus on the triceps.
setup: Bench so the bar is over your upper chest.
Close grip, elbows pointing toward your feet.
form: Bend the elbows and lower the bar toward your chin.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety stops above your chin.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar above your chin

name: Machine Dip
why: Heavy press for your triceps.
setup: Back against the pad.
form: Push down until your arms are straight.
Come back up as deep as is comfortable.
avoid: Short reps that skip the deep part.
rangeOfMotion: Handles up → arms straight

name: Triceps Dip
why: Upright dip: heavy press for your triceps.
setup: Arms straight on the bars, body upright, elbows close.
form: Lower until your upper arms are about level.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Too easy? Add weight with a dip belt.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → upper arms level

preferred.why: Loadable multi-joint triceps press; strength is specific to the lift trained.

name: Bench Dip
why: Dip with your hands on a bench behind you.
setup: Hands on a bench behind you, fingers forward.
Legs out straight, heels on the floor or another bench.
form: Lower until your upper arms are about level.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Too easy? Add a plate on your lap.
avoid: Going so deep your shoulders hurt.
Hips drifting away from the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → upper arms level

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
aliases: Close-Grip Push-Up off of a Dumbbell
why: Push-up with hands close: more triceps.
setup: Hands under your chest, close together.
Body straight.
form: Lower until your chest nearly touches your hands, elbows close.
Push up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest near your hands

name: Incline Close-Grip Push-Up
why: Easier close push-up with hands up on a bar.
setup: Hands close together on a Smith bar or bench.
Feet back, body straight.
form: Lower your chest to your hands, elbows close.
Push up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest at your hands

name: V-Bar Pushdown
why: Triceps, arms at your sides.
setup: Pulley high, V-bar.
Elbows at your sides, lean forward a little.
form: Push down until straight and squeeze.
Forearms come up just past level.
tips: The straight-arm squeeze is the point.
rangeOfMotion: Forearms level → arms straight
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Bar Pushdown
why: Straight-bar pushdown: easy to add weight.
setup: Pulley high, straight bar, hands shoulder-width.
Elbows at your sides.
form: Push down until your arms are straight.
Let your forearms come up just past level.
rangeOfMotion: Forearms level → arms straight

preferred.why: Top-rated for the outer triceps heads; easy to add weight.

name: Rope Pushdown
why: Pushdown with a rope: hands spread at the bottom.
setup: Pulley high, rope.
Elbows at your sides.
form: Push down and spread the rope ends apart.
Let your forearms come up just past level.
rangeOfMotion: Forearms level → arms straight

name: Reverse-Grip Pushdown
why: Pushdown with palms up.
setup: Pulley high, straight bar, palms facing up.
Elbows at your sides.
form: Push down until your arms are straight.
Let your forearms come up just past level.
tips: Go lighter than a normal pushdown.
rangeOfMotion: Forearms level → arms straight

name: One-arm Reverse-Grip Pushdown
why: Pushdown one arm at a time, palm up.
setup: Pulley high, single handle, palm up.
Elbow at your side.
form: Push down until your arm is straight and squeeze.
Let your forearm come up past level.
rangeOfMotion: Forearm up → arm straight
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Cross-Body Cable Triceps Extension
why: Cables crossed in front: arms straighten down and out.
setup: Stand between two high pulleys, a handle in each hand.
Cables crossed, elbows bent in front of your chest.
form: Push the handles down and out until your arms are straight, pause.
Bend back to the start.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows bent → arms straight
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Rope Overhead Tricep Extension
why: Triceps (long head) stretched overhead.
setup: Face away from the cable.
Rope behind your head, elbows in close to your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower into a deep stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Hands behind your head → arms straight

preferred.why: Arms overhead stretch the long head; grew the triceps more than pushdowns in a trial.

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension (Bar)
why: Overhead extension with a bar: easier to add weight than a rope.
setup: Face away from the cable, straight bar behind your head.
Elbows forward by your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower into a deep stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Hands behind your head → arms straight

name: Katana Cable Triceps Extension
why: One-arm overhead extension across the body.
setup: Pulley low, face away, handle behind your head on the opposite side.
Elbow up by your head.
form: Straighten your arm up and out to the side.
Lower back across into a stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Hand behind your head → arm straight

name: One-arm Overhead Cable Extension
why: Overhead extension one arm at a time.
setup: Pulley low, face away, handle behind your head.
Elbow up by your ear.
form: Straighten your arm overhead.
Lower into a deep stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Hand behind your head → arm straight

name: Kneeling Overhead Cable Extension
why: Overhead extension kneeling, upper arms resting on a bench.
setup: Bench sideways in front of a high pulley, kneel facing away.
Upper arms on the bench, bar behind your head.
form: Straighten your arms forward.
Bend back into a deep stretch.
avoid: Upper arms lifting off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Hands behind your head → arms straight

name: Seated Overhead Dumbbell Extension
why: One dumbbell overhead in both hands: long head stretched.
setup: Sit with back support, one dumbbell held in both palms behind your head.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Dumbbell behind your head → arms straight

name: Standing Overhead Dumbbell Extension
why: Standing overhead extension with one dumbbell.
setup: Stand, one dumbbell held in both palms behind your head.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Dumbbell behind your head → arms straight

name: One-arm Overhead Dumbbell Extension
why: Overhead extension one arm at a time.
setup: Sit or stand, dumbbell behind your head in one hand, elbow up.
form: Straighten your arm overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Dumbbell behind your head → arm straight

name: Standing Overhead Barbell Extension
why: Overhead extension with a bar.
setup: Stand, bar behind your head, hands a bit closer than shoulders.
Elbows up by your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the bar behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Bar behind your head → arms straight

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
aliases: Lying Close-Grip Barbell Triceps Press To Chin
why: Lying extension: hardest near the stretch.
setup: Lie flat, EZ bar on the inner grips, arms straight up.
form: Bend only your elbows and lower the bar to your forehead.
Straighten your arms.
tips: Tilt your arms back a little for a bigger stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your forehead

preferred.why: Top-rated triceps exercise: heavy load near the stretch.

name: Barbell Extension Behind the Head
aliases: Lying Close-Grip Barbell Triceps Extension Behind The Head
why: Lying extension with the bar going behind your head: big stretch.
setup: Lie flat, head near the bench end, close grip, arms straight up.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar behind your head

name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
why: Extension on an incline: long head stretched.
setup: Incline bench at 45–75°, bar overhead, hands a bit closer than shoulders.
form: Lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar behind your head

name: EZ Bar Incline Tricep Extension
why: Triceps (long head) stretched.
setup: Bench at 30–45°.
Arms straight up, tilted slightly back.
form: Bend only your elbows, lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten back up.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar behind your head

name: Decline EZ-Bar Triceps Extension
why: Skullcrusher on a decline bench.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in, EZ bar straight over you.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the bar to your forehead.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your forehead

name: Decline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Dumbbell skullcrusher on a decline bench.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in, dumbbells straight over you, palms in.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your head

name: Dumbbell Skullcrusher
why: Lying extension, each arm free.
setup: Lie flat, dumbbells straight up, palms facing in.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your head

name: Lying Dumbbell Extension (Palms Down)
why: Dumbbell skullcrusher with palms facing your feet.
setup: Lie flat, dumbbells straight up, palms facing your feet.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your head

name: One-arm Lying Dumbbell Extension (Palm Down)
aliases: One Arm Pronated Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Lying extension one arm at a time, palm toward your feet.
setup: Lie flat, one dumbbell straight up, palm toward your feet.
Free hand holds the working upper arm.
form: Bend your elbow and lower the dumbbell toward the other shoulder.
Straighten your arm.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight → dumbbell by the other shoulder

name: One-arm Lying Dumbbell Extension (Palm Up)
aliases: One Arm Supinated Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Lying extension one arm at a time, palm toward your face.
setup: Lie flat, one dumbbell straight up, palm toward your face.
Free hand holds the working upper arm.
form: Bend your elbow and lower the dumbbell to the same shoulder.
Straighten your arm.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight → dumbbell by your shoulder

name: Tate Press
why: Lying extension with elbows out, dumbbells to your chest.
setup: Lie flat, dumbbells straight up, palms toward your feet.
Elbows pointing out.
form: Bend your elbows and bring the dumbbells in and down to your chest.
Push them back up the same way.
avoid: Resting the dumbbells on your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells on your chest

name: Cable Skullcrusher
why: Lying extension with a cable: tension the whole way.
setup: Lie flat, head toward a low pulley, straight bar.
Arms straight up over your chest.
form: Bend your elbows and lower the bar to your forehead.
Straighten your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your forehead

name: Lying Rope Triceps Extension
why: Lying cable extension with a rope, forearms toward the pulley.
setup: Lie on a row bench, head toward the pulley, rope in hands.
Upper arms pointing up, elbows bent.
form: Straighten your arms and squeeze.
Bend your elbows, forearms back toward the pulley.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows bent → arms straight
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Incline Cable Triceps Extension
why: Cable extension lying on an incline, facing away from a high pulley.
setup: Incline bench, back to a high pulley, straight bar, narrow grip.
Upper arms angled up, elbows in.
form: Straighten your arms and squeeze.
Bend your elbows, bar back toward the pulley.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows bent → arms straight
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Machine Triceps Extension
why: Seated extension with the arms on a pad.
setup: Seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Upper arms flat on the pad.
form: Push the handles down until your arms are straight, pause.
Return, not all the way to the stack.
avoid: Upper arms lifting off the pad.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows bent → arms straight
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Dumbbell Kickback
aliases: Standing Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Bent-over extension: triceps fully squeezed.
setup: Bend forward, back flat, dumbbells in hand.
Upper arms at your sides, level with your back.
form: Straighten your arms back, squeeze.
Bend back to about 90°.
tips: Go light. The squeeze is the point.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows at 90° → arms straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: One-arm Dumbbell Kickback
aliases: Standing Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Kickback one arm at a time.
setup: Bend forward, free hand on a bench.
Upper arm at your side, level with your back.
form: Straighten your arm back, squeeze.
Bend back to about 90°.
tips: Go light. The squeeze is the point.
rangeOfMotion: Elbow at 90° → arm straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: Seated One-arm Dumbbell Kickback
aliases: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Kickback sitting, one arm at a time.
setup: Sit at the end of a bench, lean forward, back flat.
Upper arm at your side, level with your back.
form: Straighten your arm back, squeeze.
Bend back to about 90°.
rangeOfMotion: Elbow at 90° → arm straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: Seated Dumbbell Kickback
aliases: Seated Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Kickback sitting, both arms.
setup: Sit at the end of a bench, lean forward, back flat.
Upper arms at your sides, level with your back.
form: Straighten your arms back, squeeze.
Bend back to about 90°.
rangeOfMotion: Elbows at 90° → arms straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: Cable One-Arm Tricep Kickback
why: Triceps fully contracted.
setup: Pulley low, lean forward.
Upper arm at your side, level with the floor.
form: Straighten your arm, squeeze.
Bend back to about 90°.
tips: Go light. The squeeze is the point.
rangeOfMotion: Elbow at 90° → arm straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: Standing Cable Tricep Kickback
why: Triceps fully contracted. Leaning back keeps the cable pulling right up to lockout.
setup: Pulley high, single handle. Face the machine, free hand on the frame.
Lean back, body straight, upper arm at your side.
form: Straighten your arm down and back, squeeze.
Bend until your forearm points up at the pulley.
tips: Go light. The squeeze is the point.
Keep the same lean on every rep.
avoid: Elbow drifting forward (turns it into a pushdown).
Stopping before your arm is straight.
rangeOfMotion: Elbow at 90° → arm straight
tempo: Straighten 1 s · Hold 1 s · Bend 3 s

name: Assisted Dip Machine
heavyWhy: bodyweight with help: can't be loaded heavy
why: Dips with a counterweight helping, until you can do them on your own.
setup: Pick the help on the stack: more weight = easier.
Knees on the pad, hands on the bars, arms straight, body upright.
form: Lower until your upper arms are about level.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Take less help as you get stronger.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → upper arms level

name: Seated EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
why: Overhead extension with the bent bar, back supported.
setup: Sit with your back against an upright bench.
Bar behind your head on the angled grips, elbows up by your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the bar behind your head.
tips: The bent bar is easier on the wrists.
rangeOfMotion: Bar behind your head → arms straight

name: Standing EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
why: Overhead extension with the bent bar, standing.
setup: Stand, feet hip width, ribs down.
Bar behind your head on the angled grips, elbows up by your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the bar behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Bar behind your head → arms straight

name: Machine Overhead Triceps Extension
why: Overhead extension on a machine: easy to load, nothing to balance.
setup: Sit with your upper arms on the pads, pointing up.
Handles behind your head, elbows bent.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Bend back into a deep stretch.
avoid: Lifting your back off the pad.
rangeOfMotion: Hands behind your head → arms straight

name: Kettlebell Overhead Triceps Extension
why: Overhead extension with a kettlebell held by the handle.
setup: Stand, kettlebell by the handle sides in both hands, behind your head.
Elbows up by your ears.
form: Straighten your arms overhead.
Lower the bell behind your head.
rangeOfMotion: Bell behind your head → arms straight
